note: qnt-poss-plus (`a++ab`) disagrees with the oracle on at least subject f-aaab (\"aaab\"): the oracle (true PCRE possessive semantics) reads NOMATCH -- a++ possessively consumes all three available a's with no backtrack available to release one for the trailing literal \"ab\", and no other start offset has enough a's either. rust-regex's automaton has no backtracking to forbid in the first place (testees/rust/CLAUDE.md's own witness: `(?:a++)a` against \"aaa\" matches at [0,3) under this driver, exactly as a+ would), so its Thompson-NFA/lazy-DFA simulation of a++ab computes the SAME regular language as the non-possessive a+ab -- which backtracks the a-run down to two a's, leaving \"ab\" to match the trailing literal, and DOES match \"aaab\" whole (confirmed directly: qnt-plus-ctl, the non-possessive control over the identical subject, expects MATCH [0,4) per expectations.tsv). No exact trial count is stated (only f-aaab's shape -- an a-run immediately followed by a literal \"ab\" -- creates the possessive-vs-backtrack ambiguity among this pattern's 42 subjects; the other 41 were not individually re-verified for the SAME shape, so `gt 0` states the direction without overclaiming the count).

qnt-poss-star (`a*+b`) is a CONTROL, not a witness: anchored whole-subject, the pattern's own shape (a* then a single trailing literal `b`) forces the split -- `b` must match the last character and `a*` must match everything before it -- so possessive and greedy-with-backtrack computations can NEVER diverge for this specific pattern (no ambiguity exists to backtrack into), unlike qnt-poss-plus's trailing two-character literal `ab`. Directly confirmed on f-aaab (the one subject where the pattern's `a*b` shape applies at all): the oracle ALREADY reads MATCH [0,4) under true possessive semantics -- rust-regex's automaton computes the identical result. The other 41 subjects do not have the required trailing-`b` shape at all (oracle NOMATCH, and rust-regex's automaton has no possible different reading of a `b` that is not there); no divergence is possible on any of the 42 subjects.
